findings.summary: --plugin kept the lexicographically largest version, so of {1.9.0, 1.28.0, 1.32.0} it printed 'newest installed — kept' over 1.9.0 while marking 1.32.0 — the copy a live session executes from — as stale for rmtree. The row printed the safety guarantee it had failed to compute, causing the exact H8 harm its own docstring cites.

No containment assertion before os.remove/rmtree. A symlinked .claude defeated the string-prefix check and deleted a file outside the target while printing an in-target path; the rmdir-upward loop climbed past .claude and removed the target root itself, unannounced. The deleted set exceeded the printed set — the one property this feature promises.

is_protected_worktree failed OPEN: _git returned '' for both success-with-no-output and failure, so a missing or erroring git made worktree_paths return [] and nothing was protected — THE HARD REFUSAL evaporating silently on a repo with five linked worktrees carrying unpushed work.

uninstall and reset --repo were exit-0 no-ops in a vendored .claude/bin/ and in the plugin cache — the only two places the verbs exist to be used. The roster resolved from <repo>/scripts/, which is not in COPY_TREES and is never vendored: the file moved to bin/ to be reachable downstream, its dependency did not. Measured: 63 files vendored, 'nothing to invert', exit 0, 65 files still present.

--burn-evidence had no dry-run path: --yes gated both legality and application, so asking to preview it returned exit 2 and the next natural invocation was the irreversible one. The canonical-source refusal also covered only the repo scope, so --burn-evidence on the plugin source was not refused at all — the cheapest scope guarded, the irreversible one skipped.

uninstall --host all left .codex/hooks.json registering two PreToolUse groups pointing at scripts it had just deleted; Codex would attempt a missing file on every Edit/Write and Bash. The installer already owned the predicate.

--only was parsed and never read, so --only registry/install/assurance were advertised choices routing to nothing, and CHECKS was a write-only registry whose only reader was a test. --fix ran under --json and discarded the subprocess result, making a failed fix indistinguishable from a successful one. The dry-run listing truncated paths to 58 chars and printed two different rmtree targets as the same string. --reason was checked for truthiness and discarded.

README claimed 'Evidence is never in scope' while --repo removes playbook-yield.jsonl (gate_yield's only input), the H8 heartbeat and the lock journal — telemetry with named live consumers and two open debts depending on it. And the --shared debt claimed a mitigation ('refuses a foreign lock, names every sharing worktree') that does not exist in the code; a debt whose stated mitigation is fictional under-reports its own severity.
